survivors.title: A retired exclusion row is never revived — reinstate the source and it stays overridden forever
survivors.evidence: Executed end-to-end through mocks-driver.js ledger derive on a fixture host, editing the brief between runs: run 1 '2 total · 2 new · 0 retired'; add '- Offline mode — Later' -> '3 total · 1 new · 0 retired'; remove it -> '3 total · 0 new · 1 retired' with E3 at 'overridden 2026-09-11'; RE-ADD the same line -> '3 total · 0 new · 0 retired' and E3 still overridden. Cause: existingSources (line 117) is built from every exclusion row regardless of status, so an overridden row's note blocks the re-add, and retire has nothing to do. D2's letter sanctions it ('add is every derived entry whose source is not already some exclusion row's note', no status qualifier), so this is spec-conformant.
survivors.impact: A non-goal the team drops and later reinstates in the brief is never shown to the client again and never reaches the parking lot or the dated exclusions file, with no message. Same silent-underivable class as the bug commit 507efe4 fixed, one step further along.

survivors.title: The spec is internally inconsistent after the amendment round: two return shapes and two status vocabularies
survivors.evidence: D1 (line 35) says an exclusion row's status is 'confirmed <date>' or 'open'; D4 (line 38) now writes 'overridden <today>'. D2 (line 36) opens 'returning [{claim, source, screen|null, journey|null}]' and later says 'returns {add, retire}'. The Contracts block (lines 79-81) still shows the bare-array return. The code returns { add, retire } (mocks-exclusions.js:125) and the executed run writes 'overridden 2026-09-11'.
survivors.impact: The next reader gets two different return shapes and two different status vocabularies for the same function and row kind.

survivors.title: Six test fixtures still spell the retired non-goal grammar 'non-goal: Later'
survivors.evidence: grep -rn 'non-goal: Later' tests/ -> exclusions-route.test.js:51,:54,:127; mocks-exclusions.test.js:30; roadmap-parking-lot.test.js:111,:160. D2 now says the non-goal source carries the BRIEF LINE, never the tag. Behaviourally inert today: walk-page.js:275 treats any note that is not answer:/withdrawn: as project-wide, and the parking-lot check reads only claim.
survivors.impact: Fixtures model a row the driver can no longer produce, so a future check keyed on the note grammar would pass against inputs that cannot exist.

survivors.title: A Boundaries bullet claims this spec adds no control, but D5 ships the agree button
survivors.evidence: Boundaries bullet six reads 'This spec adds no control, so it adds no silence'. walk-page.js:286 renders <button class="wk-excl-agree" data-wk="agree">; walk.browser.js:211-216 on ok disables the button and decrements the count with no showMsg call. The only status strings are msgWhy and msgFailed, both failures — the rest of the bullet is accurate.
survivors.impact: A reader relying on Boundaries to know which shipped controls are receipt-less will miss the agree button.

survivors.title: The deviations sidecar still describes the withdrawn take-back control in the present tense
survivors.evidence: Lines 74-84 describe myNotesForJourney, [data-wk="mynote"], renderMyNotes(label) and AC-20260910-05-11 as built; a later bullet withdraws them. grep across spec/ tests/ specs/ docs/ finds those identifiers ONLY in this deviations file (lines 74-79, 97-104); zero in code or tests.
survivors.impact: Someone reading the deviations file top-down believes a client notes list exists in the player until the last bullet.
